First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometry identity 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{coth}⁡x(2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+\operatorname{csch}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{csch}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{csch}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int 2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int \operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{csch}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

cot⁡x=cos⁡xsin⁡x.

coth⁡x=cosh⁡xsinh⁡x.

q-96504.worked_solution:
$$

First, recall the following identity:

$$
\operatorname{csch}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{csch}^{2}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=2x.$ Then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u=\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=2x.$

| $x$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡2$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡9$ |

Now, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{csch}^{2}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}{csch}^{2}⁡u\,\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}{csch}^{2}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{coth}⁡u){|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡9} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡9)+\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡9}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡9}-1}+\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{{9}^{2}+1}{{9}^{2}-1}+\frac{{4}^{2}+1}{{4}^{2}-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{41}{40}+\frac{17}{15}) \\  & =\frac{13}{240}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}
$$

Now, we multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\cdot 2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-2)\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\,\text{d}x-\int 2\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x-2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-346480.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x}{2{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
q-346480.worked_solution:
$$

$$

First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x}{2{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {coth}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now we need to find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometric identity 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Then, we use the above identity to write the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {coth}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡x{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{coth}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡(1)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{e}^{2}+1}{{e}^{2}-1}-\frac{{e}^{4}+1}{{e}^{4}-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{({e}^{2}+1)^{2}-({e}^{4}+1)}{({e}^{4}-1)}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{e}^{4}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

q-352941.name: Question 5
q-352941.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}3\operatorname{sech}⁡(3x)\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
q-352941.worked_solution:
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities that correspond to the following trigonometric identities:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x},\,\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}3\operatorname{sech}⁡(3x)\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{sech}⁡(3x)\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(3x)}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(3x)}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(3x)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=3x.$ Then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=3x.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡8$ |

Now, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{sech}⁡(3x)\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\operatorname{sech}⁡(u)\operatorname{tanh}⁡(u)\,\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡(u){|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8} \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡8)+\operatorname{sech}⁡(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡8)}+1 \\  & =-\frac{1}{(\frac{8+{8}^{-1}}{2})}+1 \\  & =-\frac{1}{(\frac{65}{16})}+1 \\  & =\frac{49}{65}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
